title: Letter 25 — The Dignity of Man
attribution_note: Letter 25 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: What is man, that Thou art mindful of him

pairs.en: Behold, according to thy desire, I write thee also concerning man. But believe me, that as often as I consider concerning man, so often do I come into great wonder at the goodness and love of God toward man, so that I am moved to cry out with the Psalmist: *“LORD, what is man, that thou takest knowledge of him! or the son of man, that thou makest account of him!”* [Psalm 144:3]?

Truly a wondrous creation of God is man! All the creation of God is wondrous, but man is far more marvellous than all! Wondrous also is the Providence of God concerning him: he was created not as the other creatures, but was created by a special counsel of the Holy Trinity: *“Let us make man”* [Genesis 1:26]; man was created *“in the image of God”* and *“after his likeness”* [Genesis 1:27]. All created things are witnesses of the almighty power, goodness and wisdom of God; but man, besides this, beareth in himself the image of God. Truly a most fair beauty, a beloved comeliness, a most high dignity, a most precious nobility! Lower than God, but higher than all creatures, is man. With the image of God is man honoured. Fair is the heaven, the sun, the moon and the stars, and all the creation of God; but fairest of all is man, seeing that he beareth in himself the beauty created after the image of God.

sections.heading: The beauty of the soul after God's image

pairs.en: Consider and meditate how fair is God, the uncreated and eternal Beauty. *“O LORD my God, thou art very great; thou art clothed with honour and majesty.* *Who coverest thyself with light as with a garment”* [Psalm 104:1–2]. From this thou shalt in some measure know how fair is the human soul, created after the image of God. For the image must be like unto the Prototype.

All creation is subject unto man. *“The earth is the LORD's, and the fulness thereof”* [Psalm 24:1] serveth man; for neither unto God, nor unto the angels, nor unto themselves, but unto man alone do the creatures of God serve. But when man fell and perished, in a wondrous and incomprehensible manner was man raised up again and sought out. God Himself — which surpasseth every understanding and wonder — God Himself for man's sake came into this world filled with many woes, and of man (O the goodness and love of God toward man! O the honour and dignity of man!) of man *“took upon him the form”* [Philippians 2:7], lived upon the earth, laboured, was afflicted, suffered and died in His most holy Flesh for man.

He sent neither an angel nor a mediator, but Himself *“is come to seek and to save that which was lost”* [Luke 19:10]. So, having known the merciful, man-loving and wondrous Providence of God concerning himself, of what further mercy is man not made partaker from God! He was defiled, dishonoured, sinful, lawless, a child of wrath; but he is *“washed,” “justified in the name of the Lord Jesus”* [1 Corinthians 6:11], is made a spiritual member of the most heavenly Head — Jesus Christ; he partaketh mystically of His life-giving Body and Divine Blood; he is counted worthy to be a dwelling of God and a temple of the Holy Ghost; he is made partaker of communion with the Father and with His Son Jesus Christ, to *“be called the sons of God”* [1 John 3:1] by faith in Christ Jesus, *“heirs of God, and joint-heirs with”* Jesus *“Christ”* [Romans 8:17].

Read the apostolic epistles, and thou shalt see that all this and the rest the Holy Ghost ascribeth unto man, the true Christian. What yet is lacking unto man? With such great mercy, loving-kindness, honour and blessedness hath God made man partaker!
Behold, this is what man is, and in what honour he is with God! O that man would remember and consider this, and so honour God as he is honoured of God!

If God hath so honoured man, then who is against man? The whole world, all hell and all the devils can do nothing against man. God is in man and for man. *“If God be for us, who can be against us?”* boldly crieth out holy Paul [Romans 8:31].

sections.heading: The blessedness to come — and the ruin of it

pairs.en: But what shall be unto man in the life to come, according to the unfailing promise of God! What good, what blessedness, what honour, what glory! As a river shall continually flow his eternal blessedness, incomprehensible to the mind and unutterable by the tongue. *“Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him”* [1 Corinthians 2:9]. The people of God shall shine as the sun in the kingdom of their heavenly Father; they shall be as the angels; they shall be as gods second; they shall be kings and lords; they shall reign for ever and ever. For all this be glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Ghost, who hath so honoured and exalted our race!

Thou seest the blessedness of man. But know for certain, beloved, that man destroyeth all this blessedness when he showeth himself unthankful unto God, and worketh iniquity, and becometh lower and more wretched than every creature. Therefore take heed of sin, as of a venomous serpent, lest it deprive thee of Christian blessedness and cast thee into the most wretched estate.
